asm-001.check: Net cash omits $30.0B of long-term marketable investments
asm-001.closing_evidence: mapping.json maps short_term_investments to [AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesCurrent, AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesNoncurrent] with a rationale (5,070M + 30,019M = 35,089M; non-marketable equity investments of about $1.30B excluded). numerical/recompute/valuation.json (identical to computed/) shows short_term_investments 35,089,000,000 and net_cash 68,274,000,000 = 38,364M + 35,089M - 5,179M, which matches the balance sheet (periodic.txt lines 2032, 2050, 2052). note_rendered.md line 65 describes net cash as 'cash and cash equivalents plus short- and long-term marketable investments, less total debt (code output)'. The uncomputed 'rating would stay Neutral (according to the valuation specialist)' sentence is gone. The recomputed target price is $1,102 (+6.4%, Neutral).
asm-001.detail: valuation.json gives net_cash = cash 38,364M + short_term_investments 5,070M - debt 5,179M = 38,255M. The 10-K balance sheet (snapshot/docs/periodic.txt, line 2032) also reports 'Long-term marketable investments | 30,019' at 2026-09-03. The release balance sheet (release_ex99_1, line 312) shows the same figure. These are available-for-sale, investment-grade fixed-income securities, mostly maturing in one to five years (periodic.txt lines 2296, 2378, 2416). Management describes them as part of 'Cash and marketable investments totaled $73.45 billion' (periodic.txt line 1761). The item is material: it is about 41% of cash plus investments, almost six times total debt, and about $26 per share on 1,145M diluted shares. My own arithmetic, not code output, adds it to both the DCF and EV/Sales legs: DCF per share goes from about $847 to about $874, relative value from $1,792 to about $1,819, blended target price from $1,084 to about $1,110, and upside from 4.6% to about 7.1%. The rating probably stays Neutral, but the target price and every per-share value are understated. The generator knew about the gap: gen-valuation's report flagged it, and note.md discloses it as 'not recomputed in code here' and cites 'the valuation specialist' for the rating claim. Disclosure does not substitute for the fix, and an uncomputed claim about the rating should not be in the note. A fix needs no code change. The snapshot has AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesNoncurrent with 16 observations, latest 30,019M at 2026-09-03 (eu.py concepts --line short_term_investments). contracts.md allows a list of concepts summed per period. Non-marketable equity investments of $1.30B in other noncurrent assets (periodic.txt line 2432) can reasonably stay excluded.
asm-001.required_evidence: mapping.json maps the investments line to [AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesCurrent, AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesNoncurrent], or equivalent, with a rationale. Recomputed valuation.json then shows investments of 35,089M and net_cash of 68,274M at 2026-09-03. note.md describes net cash as cash and marketable investments less debt and drops the uncomputed 'rating would stay Neutral' claim.

asm-002.check: Refundable customer deposits ($12.9B) not considered as a debt-like claim
asm-002.closing_evidence: The valuation_inputs.json net_cash rationale states that the $12.895B noncurrent customer contract liabilities (F-3212bef088) are excluded as operating contract liabilities. It quotes the no-significant-financing-component language (periodic.txt line 2344, verified verbatim) and the conditional-return terms (line 1763, verified). It acknowledges the counter-arguments: the financing inflow sits in cash, and repayment falls in 2029-2031, inside DCF years 3-5. It gives an analyst-arithmetic sensitivity of about $11 per share. The WACC rationale no longer calls debt 'small' without qualification. note_rendered.md line 68 carries a labelled valuation caveat, and line 75 flags the treatment as a judgment that favours the shares.
asm-002.detail: The balance sheet shows 'Noncurrent customer contract liabilities | 12,895' (periodic.txt line 2056; $142M a year earlier). These are mainly customer deposits under the strategic customer agreements, received as a $12.75B financing inflow in FY2026 (line 1842; cash flow line 2228). The deposits are returned if customers meet their purchase commitments, and 'Nearly all of the deposits are scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031' (line 2961). That falls inside DCF years 3-5. Reported cash includes this money, but neither net cash nor the FCF path reflects the repayment. The WACC rationale also calls debt 'small ($5.179B ...)' without mentioning these deposits. The balance sheet does not label them debt, so excluding them is a defensible judgment. The impact is about $11 per share, roughly 1% of the target price. The rationale should acknowledge the exclusion, and the note should mention it as a valuation caveat.
asm-002.required_evidence: valuation_inputs.json rationale, ideally also the note, states how the $12.9B refundable customer deposits are treated (excluded as operating liabilities, or deducted as debt-like) and why.

asm-003.check: Year-1 FCF margin rationale ignores the guided capex and working capital
asm-003.closing_evidence: Year-1 FCF margin is lowered from 55% to 50% (valuation.json dcf.fcf[0] = $134.75B on $269.50B). The fcf_margin rationale quotes the capex outlook verbatim (checked against periodic.txt line 1771). It reconciles year 1 as labelled analyst arithmetic: NTM net income $188.7B (matches forecast.json ntm.net_income 188,719M) + D&A ~$12B (FY2026 $9.503B, line 2187) + SBC ~$1.5B - net capex ~$55B - working capital ~$12B (receivables $36.197B, line 2024) = ~$135B, or 50%. It also gives a 47-53.5% range.
asm-003.detail: Year-1 FCF margin is 55%, which gives FCF of $148.2B on NTM revenue of $269.5B. The rationale anchors it on history (FY2026 44.3%, FY2026Q4 60.6% in a 14-week quarter) and says capex keeps rising. It does not cite the 10-K's explicit capex outlook: 'approximately $11.5 billion in the first quarter of 2027, approximately $25 billion in the first six months of 2027, and higher in the second half of 2027' (periodic.txt line 1771). My rough check, not code output: NTM net income $188.7B plus D&A of about $10B (FY2026 $9.5B, line 2187) minus capex of at least about $50B gives about $148B, or 55%, only if working capital is zero. Receivables rose from $9.3B to $36.2B in FY2026, so working-capital absorption is likely while revenue grows. FY2026Q4 CFO was also helped by noncurrent Pillar Two taxes payable (line 1832). 55% is at the top of the plausible range. It needs the guided capex in its support, or a small reduction.
asm-003.required_evidence: The fcf_margin rationale cites the FY2027 capex guidance (as a quote) and reconciles the year-1 margin with NTM net income + D&A - guided capex - working capital, or lowers the year-1 margin accordingly.

asm-004.check: Pillar Two noncurrent income taxes payable ($9.82B) is not addressed in the net cash or FCF rationale
asm-004.detail: Not repaired: the candidate is unchanged since review 1 (valuation_inputs.json sha256 f228676b... and note.md cdf16378... match generator/manifest.json, and computed/ equals numerical/recompute/). I re-checked this in a fresh context. The 10-K says 'Other noncurrent liabilities included $9.82 billion and $648 million related to income taxes payable as of September 3, 2026 and August 28, 2025, respectively' (periodic.txt line 3101). MD&A ties the increase to Pillar Two: 'higher noncurrent income taxes payable related to the implementation of Pillar Two' (line 1832). The $9.03B FY2026 Singapore top-up tax is at line 3099. History shows FY2026Q4 CFO of $43.973B, which carries most of the deferral. FY2026 FCF excluding the roughly $9.6B other-noncurrent-liabilities inflow would be about 37% of revenue rather than 44.3% (my arithmetic). The fcf_margin rationale says Q4 CFO was 'flattered' by this item and that 'A recurring Pillar Two tax deferral is possible upside but is not assumed'. But neither fcf_margin nor net_cash says how the $9.82B balance already accrued is treated. That cash sits in reported cash, so it is inside net cash of $68.274B. It is not deducted, and its payment is not in the FCF path. Size, my own arithmetic and not code output: $9.82B / 1,145M diluted shares is about $8.6 per share on both legs. The blended value would be about $1,093, upside about +5.6%, and the rating stays Neutral. This is a judgment of the same kind as the customer deposits (asm-002), so it should be stated. Minor.
asm-004.required_evidence: The valuation_inputs.json net_cash or fcf_margin rationale states how the $9.82B noncurrent income taxes payable is treated: deducted as debt-like, paid inside the FCF path, or a rolling operating liability with no adjustment. It gives the reason and an approximate per-share sensitivity labelled as analyst arithmetic.

asm-005.check: The rating depends on the DCF/EV-Sales weight, and the note does not show the relative-value leg
asm-005.detail: Not repaired: the candidate is unchanged since review 1. I re-verified the figures. Code output (numerical/recompute/valuation.json): DCF $862.83 per share and relative EV/Sales $1,818.58 per share (15.121x x $133.188B + $68.274B, over 1,145M shares). At dcf_weight 0.75 the blend is $1,101.77, TP $1,102, +6.39%, Neutral. My own arithmetic, not code output: Outperform needs TP >= $1,191.22, which holds at a DCF weight of about 0.656 or less. Underperform needs TP <= $932.26, which holds at a weight of about 0.927 or more. The note (note_rendered.md, Model and valuation section) still shows only the DCF per-share value and the peer multiple. It does not show the relative-value leg, the 75/25 weights, or that the rating rests on the weighting. Constraint on the repair: values.json (38 keys) has no key for relative_per_share or dcf_weight, so under the untagged-number gate the writer cannot show those numbers until the code owner adds the keys. A qualitative sentence, labelled our view, saying the two methods diverge widely and the rating is sensitive to the weighting needs no new key and can be added now. Minor; the inputs are inside policy and the dcf_weight rationale exists.
asm-005.required_evidence: note.md shows the relative-value per-share figure and the DCF/relative weights through code values (if values.json provides keys for them), and adds one sentence, labelled analyst judgment, saying the rating is sensitive to the weighting.

cmp-001.closing_evidence: numerical/recompute/note_rendered.md line 5 and Disclosures lines 82-83 now name the Form 10-K, accession 0000723125-26-000023 (its acceptance sets the cutoff of 2026-10-09 12:21 UTC), and separately 'The earnings release, furnished separately on Form 8-K, accession 0000723125-26-000018, in September 2026, before the 10-K', as the source of the guidance, CEO statement and dividend quote. The accession comes from the code key values.json#release_accession (source snapshot/manifest.json), so the writer typed no digits. It matches snapshot/manifest.json (docs/release_ex99_1 earnings release.txt -> 0000723125-26-000018) and snapshot/filings.json (8-K, items 2.02,9.01, accepted 2026-09-30T20:02:22Z, before the cutoff). cmp-001.detail: The Disclosures section (note.md line 74) says: 'SEC EDGAR filing accession 0000723125-26-000023 (Form 10-K and the accompanying earnings release exhibit)'. The earnings release is not an exhibit to the 10-K. snapshot/manifest.json lists docs/release_ex99_1 earnings release.txt as accession 0000723125-26-000018 (document a2026q4ex991-pressrelease.htm), and snapshot/filings.json shows that accession is a Form 8-K (items 2.02, 9.01) accepted 2026-09-30T20:02:22Z. A full fix may need a code-provided key such as release_accession. prov-001.detail: The texts of quotes Q-1 to Q-4 in narrative.json are copied from the release's flattened table and contain the separator ' | | ' (e.g. Q-2 'Approximately 85.95% | | Approximately 86.25%'). note.md puts these quotes inside a three-column Markdown table, so each rendered row (computed/note_rendered.md lines 32-35) contains five cells instead of three. A GFM renderer ignores the extra cells, so the published table shows only the GAAP half of each quote with an unclosed quotation mark ('“Approximately 85.95%'), an empty cell, and no 'Code value used' column at all. As a result the non-GAAP guidance wording and all of the code-generated guidance figures ($61.5bn midpoint, 86.0% / 86.2%, $2.3bn / $2.1bn, $37.84 / $38.15) disappear from the table. The quotes are then shown truncated in a way the source does not support, and the evidence trail from quote to code value is broken. The underlying values themselves are correct; I checked them against release lines 161-178.

prov-004.check: Claim that including long-term marketable investments leaves the rating unchanged is unquantified and attributed to a specialist rather than to evidence
prov-004.closing_evidence: The specialist-attributed 'rating would stay Neutral (not recomputed in code here)' sentence is gone. grep finds no 'specialist' in note.md. Net cash is now the code value {{net_cash}} = $68.3bn (valuation.json net_cash 68,274M = cash 38,364M (F-455b2cbdf8) + investments 35,089M (S-0f9cbd5118 = F-e8f2f41b64 5,070M + F-5368223b24 30,019M) - debt 5,179M (S-0a86662e54 = F-ca07e4ae2b 491M + F-bce6b48da4 4,688M)). prov-005.check: Customer-deposit caveat paraphrases the 10-K more strongly than the source and is not quote-backed
prov-005.detail: The candidate is unchanged since review 1. The sha256 of generator/note.md (cdf16378...) and of narrative.json (b0a82e15...) still match manifest.json, which carries request_id gen-20261115T080625-5b263d. The 'Valuation caveat' paragraph in note.md (rendered at computed/note_rendered.md line 68) still says 'a deposit is returned only if the customer meets its minimum purchase commitments'. The 10-K says deposits 'are returned to the customer if the customer meets the minimum purchase commitments. If the customer does not meet the minimum purchase commitments, we may retain all or a portion of the deposit' (periodic.txt line 1763). Line 2344 adds 'If not, we may retain all, or a portion of the deposit which will be recognized as revenue'. 'May retain all or a portion' allows a partial return when the commitment is missed, so 'only if' overstates the condition. The paragraph also still attributes 'nearly all of the deposits are scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031' to the 10-K without a [[Q-id]]. No such quote exists among Q-1..Q-17 in narrative.json. The paraphrase is accurate: periodic.txt line 2961 reads verbatim 'Nearly all of the deposits are scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031.' A reader still cannot check it through the quote trail. The judgment (treat the deposits as operating liabilities) is labelled as our view and is not affected. No figure changes.
prov-005.required_evidence: The caveat says 'returned if the customer meets ...' (or adds that the company may retain all or a portion otherwise) instead of 'only if'. Ideally the repayment-timing statement is cited through a verbatim narrative quote, e.g. 'Nearly all of the deposits are scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031.'
